<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="ffff403dc-5bf5-4977-a6cf-c5ec1db784c0">
Genesis Plaza is owned by two tenants-in-common, NetREIT Genesis and NetREIT Genessis II, each of which own 57% and 43%, respectively, and we beneficially own an aggregate of 92.0%, based on our ownership of each entity. We have 100% ownership of NetREIT Genesis and 81.5% ownership of NetREIT Genesis II, and we have control of both entities. During July 2024, the Company completed a minority ownership conversion option as result of a death in a noncontrolling trust within NetREIT Genesis II.  The Company issued the trust 86,232 shares of SQFT Series A Common Stock in exchange for their 36.4% ownership in NetREIT Genesis II, as per the original exchange agreement.</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="f22b49efa-f7d7-4e56-9a41-7ba817c63105">Includes land, buildings and improvements, cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash, current receivables, deferred rent receivables and deferred leasing costs and other related intangible assets, all shown on a net basis.</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="ff7493759-8bf5-4ccb-b359-b186c87dfdb8">The non-recourse loan on the Dakota Center property matured on July 6, 2024. During December 2024, the lender agreed to the broker the Company would use to sell the property to settle the non-recourse debt. During July 2025, the lender approved a purchase offer from a third party for $5,125,000.  In connection with the approved sale, we have impaired the property&#8217;s book value and recorded an impairment charge of approximately $3.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025. The sale was completed on  January 14, 2026, resulting in a net gain of approximately $0.6 million, net of closing costs. </ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="fa454cd5f-7842-4b92-a160-40cb84397dc2">As of December 31, 2025, there were five model homes included as real estate assets held for sale. Our model homes have stand-alone mortgage notes at interest rates ranging from 5.94% to 8.0% per annum as of December 31, 2025.</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="f554b9fbb-d89e-4384-a208-791b7719e4b2">Includes lease intangibles and the land purchase option related to property acquisitions.</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="f5c15547c-c455-4cc9-845b-9284cdab1929">The non-recourse loan on the Dakota Center property matured on July 6, 2024. During December 2024, the lender agreed to the broker the Company would use to sell the property to settle the non-recourse debt. As of March 31, 2026, the property was included in the real estate assets held for sale, net on the consolidated balance sheet. During July 2025, the lender approved a purchase offer from a third party for $5,125,000.  In connection with the approved sale, we have impaired the property&#8217;s book value and recorded an impairment charge of approximately $3.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025. The sale was completed on  January 14, 2026, resulting in a net gain of approximately $0.6 million, net of closing costs. See Note 4. Real Estate Assets above for further discussion on impairment of the property.</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="f17f95f46-1bf7-4a1c-a9c5-5776181e0a3e">As of March 31, 2026, there were four model homes included as real estate assets held for sale. Our model homes have stand-alone mortgage notes at interest rates ranging from 5.76% to 8.0% per annum as of  March 31, 2026</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="ffe417cd3-eecd-4b12-a847-f60c3e183e85">Includes Model Homes listed as held for sale as of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025.  During the three months ended March 31, 2026, we recorded an impairment charge for model homes totaling $75,639, which reflects the estimated sales prices for these specific model homes.  The short hold period, less than two years, and the builder changing their model style after we purchased the homes, contributed to the lower-than-expected sales price.</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="f2ea5011f-b656-4528-ae3d-1cc346e6a17b">During January 2026, the Company received notice that the Company's failure to repay in full by January 5, 2026 the indebtedness related to the loan agreement governing Shea Center II had triggered a default event. On February 13, 2026, the Company received notification that the Shea Center II property governed by the loan agreement was moved into receivership, which will fulfill its obligation for this non-recourse loan.  The foreclosure sale and public auction is scheduled for June 17, 2026.  During the three months ended March 31, 2026, the Company completed the transfer of the real estate to lender in connection with a loan default. At the time of transfer, cash of approximately $2.3 million was held in a lender-controlled lockbox and was legally restricted for the benefit of the lender. The restricted cash was retained by the lender upon receivership, and the Company did not receive any cash proceeds from the transaction. Prior to the foreclosure, the restricted cash was presented within Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash on the consolidated balance sheet. The receivership resulted in the derecognition of real estate, restricted cash, and the related mortgage debt. The Company recognized a loss on foreclosure of approximately $2.4 million. The transaction represents a noncash investing and financing activity on the statement of cash flow.</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="fde7ba38b-bafa-4005-a322-d91e002610db">As of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, includes approximately $7.4 million and $8.6 million, respectively, of assets related to consolidated variable interest entities that can be used only to settle obligations of the consolidated variable interest entities.</ix:footnote>
<ix:footnote xml:lang="en-us" id="f3bc2f745-49fb-44ce-a078-9c4edb4e3714">A portion of the proceeds from the sale of Highland Court were used in like-kind exchange transactions pursued under Section 1031 of the Code for the acquisition of our Mandolin property. Mandolin is owned by NetREIT Palm Self-Storage LP, through its wholly owned subsidiary, NetREIT Highland LLC, and the Company is the sole general partner and owns 61.3% of NetREIT Palm Self-Storage LP.</ix:footnote>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> ORGANIZATION AND BASIS OF PRESENTATION</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Organization.&#160;</i></b>Presidio Property Trust, Inc. ("we", "our", "us" or the "Company") is an internally-managed real estate investment trust ("REIT"), with holdings in office, industrial, retail and model home properties. We were incorporated in the State of California on <em style="font: inherit;"> September 28, 1999, </em>and in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2010, </em>we reincorporated as a Maryland corporation. In <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2017, </em>we changed our name from "NetREIT, Inc." to "Presidio Property Trust, Inc." Through Presidio Property Trust, Inc., its subsidiaries, and its partnerships, we own&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c146049065" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-CommercialPropertyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstatePropertiesFeeSimple" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;commercial properties in fee interest, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049066">two</span> of which we own as a partial interest in various affiliates, in which we serve as general partner, member and/or manager, and a special purpose acquisition company (until deconsolidation in <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2023) </em>as noted below.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company or <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of its affiliates operates the following partnerships during the periods covered by these&#160;consolidated financial statements:</p>
   <p style="margin: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">&#8226;</td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company is the sole general partner and limited partner in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049068">two</span> limited partnerships (NetREIT Palm Self-Storage LP and NetREIT Casa Grande LP), both of which, as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, had ownership interests in an entity that owns income producing real estate. The Company refers to these entities collectively as the "NetREIT Partnerships".</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman;">&#160;</td><td style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman;">&#160;</td></tr>

The Company refers to these entities collectively as the "Model Home Partnerships".&#160;As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#202,</em> LP, Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#203,</em> LP, Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#204,</em> LP, and Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#206,</em> LP had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> remaining assets.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has determined that the limited partnerships, in which it owns less than <em style="font: inherit;">100%,</em> should be included in the Company's consolidated financial statements as the Company directs their activities and has control of such limited partnerships.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have elected to be taxed as a REIT under Sections <em style="font: inherit;">856</em> through <em style="font: inherit;">860</em> of the Internal Revenue Code of <em style="font: inherit;">1986,</em> as amended (the "Code"), for federal income tax purposes. To maintain our qualification as a REIT, we are required to distribute at least <em style="font: inherit;">90%</em> of our REIT taxable income to our stockholders and meet the various other requirements imposed by the Code relating to such matters as operating results, asset holdings, distribution levels, and diversity of stock ownership. Provided we maintain our qualification for taxation as a REIT, we are generally <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to corporate-level income tax on the earnings distributed currently to our stockholders that we derive from our REIT qualifying activities. If we fail to maintain our qualification as a REIT in any taxable year and are unable to avail ourselves of certain savings provisions set forth in the Code, all our taxable income would be subject to federal income tax at regular corporate rates, including any applicable alternative minimum tax. We are subject to certain state and local income taxes.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We, together with <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of our entities, have elected to treat certain subsidiaries as a taxable REIT subsidiary (a "TRS") for federal income tax purposes. Certain activities that we undertake must be conducted by a TRS, such as non-customary services for our commercial tenants, and holding assets that we cannot hold directly. A TRS is subject to federal and state income taxes. The Company has concluded that there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant uncertain tax positions requiring recognition in its financial statements. Neither the Company nor its subsidiaries have been assessed any significant interest or penalties for tax positions by any tax jurisdictions.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Effective on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 19, 2025, </em>the Company amended its charter by filing&#160;Articles of Amendment with the&#160;State Department of Assessments and&#160;Taxation of Maryland in order to effect a <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-for-<ix:nonFraction id="c146049087" contextRef="d_2025-05-19_2025-05-19_NonmonetaryTransactionTypeAxis-ReverseStockSplitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10</ix:nonFraction> reverse stock split of its outstanding shares of common stock (the &#8220;Reverse Stock Split&#8221;). As a result of the Reverse Stock Split, every <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock issued or outstanding were automatically reclassified into <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> new share of common stock, par value $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049090" contextRef="i_2025-05-19" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.10</ix:nonFraction> per share,&#160;subject to the treatment of fractional shares as described below, without any action on the part of the holders. All historical share and per-share amounts reflected throughout the accompanying consolidated financial statements and other financial information in this Quarterly Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q have been retroactively adjusted to reflect the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Reverse Stock Split as if the split occurred as of the earliest period presented. The Reverse Stock Split did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> affect the number of authorized shares of common stock. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> fractional shares were issued in connection with the Reverse Stock Split. Stockholders who would otherwise have been entitled to receive fractional shares as a result of the Reverse Stock Split were rounded up to the nearest whole share.&#160;All equity awards and warrants outstanding immediately prior to the Reverse Stock Split were proportionately adjusted to reflect the Reverse Stock Split. Effective immediately after the Reverse Stock Split, the Company decreased the par value of the shares of Series A Common Stock from $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049095" contextRef="i_2025-05-18_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesACommonStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.10</ix:nonFraction> per share back to $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049096" contextRef="i_2025-05-19_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesACommonStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.01</ix:nonFraction> per share.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Liquidity.&#160;</span></i></b><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">The Company's anticipated future sources of liquidity <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include existing cash and cash equivalents, cash flows from operations, refinancing of existing mortgages, future real estate sales, new borrowings, and the sale of equity or debt securities.&#160;Future capital needs include paying down existing borrowings, maintaining our existing properties, funding&#160;tenant improvements on our commercial buildings, p</span><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">aying lease commissions (to the extent they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> covered by lender-held reserve deposits), and the payment of dividends to our stockholders. The Company is also seeking investments that are likely to produce income and achieve long-term gains in order to pay dividends to our stockholders. To ensure that we can effectively execute these objectives, we routinely review our liquidity requirements and continually evaluate all potential sources of liquidity. I</span>f necessary, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>seek other short-term liquidity alternatives, such as bridge loans, refinancing property loans or a bank line&#160;of credit depending on&#160;the credit environment.&#160;See Note <em style="font: inherit;">11</em> Stockholders' Equity for additional information on sale of securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Short-term liquidity needs include paying our current operating costs, satisfying the debt service requirements of existing mortgages, completing <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">ant improvements o</span><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">n our commercial buildings, paying leasing commissions, distributions to noncontrolling interests, and funding dividends, if any, to stockholders.&#160;Future principal payments due on mortgage notes payable, during the last <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> quarters of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;and in the year ending&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2027 </em>total approximately </span>$<ix:nonFraction id="c146049102" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-MortgageNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalRemainderOfFiscalYear" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">20.4</ix:nonFraction> million<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c146049103" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-MortgageNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.4</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, of which&#160;</span>$<ix:nonFraction id="c146049104" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-MortgageNotesMember_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomePropertiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalRemainderOfFiscalYear" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.8</ix:nonFraction> million<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; Additional principal payments will be made with cash flows from ongoing operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As the Company continues its operations, it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>re-finance or seek additional financing. However, there can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that any such re-financing or additional financing will be available to the Company on acceptable terms, if at all. If events or circumstances occur such that the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> obtain additional funding, it will most likely be required to reduce its plans and/or certain discretionary spending, which could have a material adverse effect on the Company's ability to achieve its intended business objectives. Management believes that the combination of working capital on hand and the ability to refinance commercial and model home mortgages will fund operations through at least the next <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months from the date of the issuance of these unaudited interim financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Segments. </i></b>The Company acquires and operates income producing properties in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049112">three</span> business segments including Office/Industrial Properties, Model Home Properties and Retail Properties. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">13.</em> &#8220;Segments&#8221;.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Concentration. </i></b>Concentration of credit risk with respect to tenant receivables is limited due to the large number of tenants comprising the Company&#8217;s rental revenue.&#160;We have <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049114">three</span> commercial properties located in Colorado, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049115">three</span> in North Dakota,&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049116">one</span> in Southern California, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049117">one</span> in Texas and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049118">one</span> in Maryland. Our model home properties are concentrated in Texas with a few model homes in Alabama, Tennessee and Arizona.&#160;We had <ix:nonFraction id="c146049119" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-SalesRevenueNetMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">one</ix:nonFraction> of our homebuilders&#160;accounts for approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c146049120" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-SalesRevenueNetMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-OneHomebuilderMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">17.17</ix:nonFraction>% of our total revenue for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>and accounted for <ix:nonFraction id="c146049122" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomePropertiesMember_ShareBasedGoodsAndNonemployeeServicesTransactionBySupplierAxis-OneHomebuilderMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">52</ix:nonFraction> out of <ix:nonFraction id="c146049123" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomePropertiesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">75</ix:nonFraction> of our model home leases as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">2.</em> SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">There have been <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant changes to the Company&#8217;s accounting policies since it filed its audited financial statements in the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;year end&#160;Annual Report. For further information about the Company&#8217;s accounting policies, refer to the Company&#8217;s&#160;consolidated financial statements and notes thereto for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, included in the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;year end&#160;Annual Report.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055745" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Basis of Presentation. </i></b>The accompanying&#160;consolidated financial statements have been prepared by the Company's management in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) for interim financial statements and the instructions to Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q and Article <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> of Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X.</em> Certain information and footnote disclosures required for annual consolidated financial statements have been&#160;excluded pursuant to rules and regulations of the SEC. In the opinion of management, the accompanying&#160;consolidated financial statements reflect all adjustments of a normal and recurring nature that are considered necessary for a fair presentation of our financial position as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, as well as&#160;results of our operations, and cash<b><i> </i></b>flows as of, and for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively. However, the results of operations for the interim periods are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of the results that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be expected for the year ending <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2026</em>,&#160;due to real estate market fluctuations, available mortgage lending rates and&#160;other unknown factors. These&#160;consolidated financial statements should be read in conjunction with the audited financial statements and notes thereto included in the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;year end&#160;Annual Report. The&#160;consolidated balance sheet<b><i> </i></b>as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em><b><i>&#160;</i></b>has been derived from the audited consolidated financial statements included in the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;year end&#160;Annual Report.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055746" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Principles of Consolidation</i></b>.&#160;The accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Presidio Property Trust, Inc. and its subsidiaries, NetREIT Advisors, LLC and Dubose Advisors LLC (collectively, the &#8220;Advisors&#8221;). The&#160;consolidated&#160;financial statements also include the results of the NetREIT Partnerships and&#160;the Model Home Partnerships.&#160;As used herein, references to the &#8220;Company&#8221; include references to Presidio Property Trust, Inc., its subsidiaries<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">, and the partnerships. All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">The Company classifies the noncontrolling interests in the NetREIT Partnerships as part of</span>&#160;<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">consolid</span><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">ated net (loss) in</span>come&#160;in <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;and has i</span>ncluded the accumulated amount of noncontrolling interests as part of equity since inception in <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2010. </em>If a change in ownership of a consolidated subsidiary results in loss of control and deconsolidation, any retained ownership interest will be remeasured, with the gain or loss reported in the&#160;consolidated statements of operations. Management has evaluated the noncontrolling interests and determined that they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contain any redemption features.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c146055747" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Use of Estimates</i></b>.&#160;The&#160;consolidated financial statements were prepared in conformity with U.S. GAAP, which requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting period. Significant estimates include&#160;private warrants,&#160;the allocation of purchase price paid for property acquisitions between the components of land, building and intangible assets acquired including their useful lives,&#160;valuation of long-lived assets, and the allowance for doubtful accounts, which is based on an evaluation of the tenants&#8217; ability to pay. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:RealEstatePolicyTextBlock" id="c146055748" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Real Estate Assets and Lease Intangibles. </i></b>Land, buildings and improvements are recorded at cost, including tenant improvements and lease acquisition costs (including leasing commissions, space planning fees, and legal fees). The Company capitalizes any expenditure that replaces, improves, or otherwise extends the economic life of an asset, while ordinary repairs and maintenance are expensed as incurred. The Company allocates the purchase price of acquired properties between the acquired tangible assets and liabilities (consisting of land, buildings, tenant improvements, and long-term debt) and identified intangible assets and liabilities (including the value of above-market and below-market leases, the value of in-place leases, unamortized lease origination costs and tenant relationships), in each case based on their respective fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The Company allocates the purchase price to tangible assets of an acquired property based on the estimated fair values of those tangible assets, assuming the property was vacant. Estimates of fair value for land, building and building improvements are based on many factors, including, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, comparisons to other properties sold in the same geographic area and independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party valuations. In estimating the fair values of the tangible assets, intangible assets, and liabilities acquired, the Company also considers information obtained about each property as a result of its pre&#8209;acquisition due diligence, marketing and leasing activities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The value allocated to acquired lease intangibles is based on management&#8217;s evaluation of the specific characteristics of each tenant&#8217;s lease. Characteristics considered by management in allocating these values include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited, to the nature and extent of the existing business relationships with the tenant, growth prospects for developing new business with the tenant, the remaining term of the lease,&#160;the t<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">enant&#8217;s credit quality, and other factors.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="sqft:DeferredLeasingCostsPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055749" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Deferred Leasing Costs. </span></i></b><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Costs incurred in connection with successful</span> property leases are capitalized as deferred leasing costs and amortized to leasing commission expense on a straight-line basis over the terms of the related leases which generally range from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049198">one</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049199">five</span> years. If management determines the estimated remaining life of the respective lease has changed, the amortization period is adjusted. At </span><em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;and&#160;</span><em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">, the Company had net deferred leasing costs of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049201" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCostsCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049202" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCostsCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.&#160;Total amortization expense for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> was approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c146049207" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseInitialDirectCostExpenseOverTerm" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">83,447</ix:nonFraction> and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c146049208" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseInitialDirectCostExpenseOverTerm" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">134,776</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055750" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Cash, Cash Equivalents and Restricted Cash.&#160;</i></b>At <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we had approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c146049209" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.2</ix:nonFraction> million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c146049211" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.4</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, respectively, of which approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c146049212" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestrictedCash" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.6</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049213" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestrictedCash" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.7</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;represented restricted cash, respectively. The Company considers all short-term, highly liquid investments that are both readily convertible to cash and have an original maturity of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months or less at the date of purchase to be cash equivalents. Items classified as cash equivalents include money market funds and short-term bonds. Cash balances in individual banks <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>exceed the federally insured limit of <em style="font: inherit;">$250,000</em> by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC"). <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> losses have been experienced related to such accounts. Restricted cash consists of cash held in escrow by lenders pursuant to certain loan agreements, which are for payment of property taxes, insurance, leasing costs, future debt payments,&#160;and capital expenditures.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DiscontinuedOperationsPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055751" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Real Estate Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations.</i></b>&#160;We generally reclassify assets to "held for sale" when the disposition has been approved, it is available for immediate sale in its present condition, we are actively&#160;seeking a buyer, and the disposition is considered probable within <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year.&#160;Additionally, real estate sold during the current period is classified as &#8220;real estate assets held for sale&#8221; for all prior periods presented in the accompanying&#160;consolidated financial statements. Mortgage notes payable related to the real estate sold during the current period are&#160;classified as &#8220;mortgage notes payable related to properties held for sale&#8221; for all prior periods presented in the accompanying&#160;consolidated financial statements.&#160;Additionally, we record the operating results related to real estate that has been disposed of as discontinued operations&#160;for all periods presented if the operations have been eliminated and represent a strategic shift and we will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have any significant continuing involvement in the operations of the property following the sale.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>,&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049222">four</span>&#160;model homes were classified as "held for sale".</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DeferredChargesPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055752" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Deferred Offering Costs.</span></i></b><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span>Deferred offering costs represent legal, accounting and other direct costs related to our&#160;offerings. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;and&#160;</span><em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">we had deferred offering costs of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049223" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredOfferingCosts" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">287,666</ix:nonFraction> and $</span><ix:nonFraction id="c146049225" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredOfferingCosts" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">279,603</ix:nonFraction><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">, respectively.&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055753" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff">Impairments of Real Estate Assets. </span></i></b>We regularly review for impairment on a property-by-property basis. Impairment is recognized on a property&#160;held for use when the expected undiscounted cash flows for a property are less than the carrying amount at which time the property is written-down to fair value. Impairment is recognized on a property held for sale when the fair value less costs to sell is less than the carrying amount. The calculation of both discounted and undiscounted cash flows requires management to make estimates of future cash flows that are determined based on a number of inputs and assumptions such as the intended hold period, market rental rates, leasing assumptions, capitalization rates and discount rates.&#160;Actual results could be significantly different from the estimates. Although our strategy is to hold our properties over the long-term, if our strategy changes or market conditions otherwise dictate an earlier sale date, an impairment loss <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be recognized to reduce the property to fair value and such loss could be material.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

      We review the carrying value of each of our real estate properties regularly&#160;to determine if circumstances indicate an impairment in the carrying value of these investments exists. During the&#160;
     <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we recognized&#160;non-cash impairment charges of approximately
     $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049230" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-CommercialPropertyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfRealEstate" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">524,373</ix:nonFraction>&#160;&#160;and&#160;

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055754" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Fair Value Measurements</i></b>.&#160;Certain assets and liabilities are required to be carried at fair value, or if long-lived assets are deemed to be impaired, to be adjusted to reflect this condition. The guidance requires disclosure of fair values calculated under each level of inputs within the following hierarchy:</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical assets or liabilities;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> quoted prices for similar instruments in active markets, quoted prices for identical or similar instruments in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active, and model-derived valuations in which significant inputs and significant value drivers are observable in active markets; and</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em> prices or valuation techniques where little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market data is available that requires inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In instances where the market for a financial instrument is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;active, regardless of the availability of a nonbinding quoted market price, observable inputs might <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;be relevant and could require us to make a significant adjustment to derive a fair value measurement.&#160;Additionally, in an inactive market, a market price quoted from an independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party <em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>rely more on models with inputs based on information available only to that independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party. When we determine the market for a financial instrument owned by us to be illiquid or when market transactions for similar instruments do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;appear orderly, we use several valuation sources (including internal valuations, discounted cash flow analysis and quoted market prices) and establish a fair value by assigning weights to the various valuation sources.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">When&#160;determining the fair value of real estate assets, goodwill and other liabilities&#160;the Company refers to the guidance in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820.</em> The term &#8220;Fair Value&#8221; is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date (ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20</em>). In particular, ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em> prescribes that the measurement of the Fair Value of an asset or liability should be based on assumptions that market participants would use when pricing the asset or liability. Accordingly, the Company&#8217;s determination of the Fair Value measurements detailed above is based on the price that would be received to sell an asset or transfer a liability at the measurement date, assuming a transaction takes place at that date (i.e., an exit price).</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Additionally, in an inactive market, a market price quoted from an independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party <em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>rely more on models with inputs based on information available only to that independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party. When we determine the market for a financial instrument owned by us to be illiquid or when market transactions for similar instruments do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;appear orderly, we use several valuation sources (including internal valuations, discounted cash flow analysis and quoted market prices) and establish a fair value by assigning weights to the various valuation sources.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, we did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049257">not</span> hold any&#160;marketable securities,&#160;excluding our investments in common stock warrants of Conduit Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (&#8220;Conduit&#8221;).&#160;As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049259">not</span> hold any&#160;marketable securities&#160;(excluding our investments in Conduit's common stock and common stock warrants).&#160;There were <ix:nonFraction id="c146049260" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LiabilitiesFairValueDisclosure" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;financial liabilities measured at fair value as&#160;of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em><i>.</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Private CDT Warrants fair value, using Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs, was <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> for both periods, and is included in the total&#160;Investment in Conduit Pharmaceuticals marketable securities on the consolidated balance sheets.&#160;Our investments in Conduit's&#160;public common stock warrants (CDTTW)&#160;presented on the consolidated balance sheets&#160;were measured at fair value using Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> market prices,&#160;taking into account the adoption of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em>&#160;Fair Value Measurement of Equity Securities Subject to Contractual Sale Restrictions,&#160;and totaled approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049269" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-ConduitPharmaceuticalsIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNiCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5,885</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049270" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-ConduitPharmaceuticalsIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNiCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,900</ix:nonFraction> as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively. The adjustments to the fair value of our investment in Conduit Pharmaceuticals marketable securities are recorded in net loss in Conduit Pharmaceuticals marketable securities on our&#160;consolidated statement of operations.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c146055755" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Earnings per share (</i></b>&#8220;<b style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i>EPS</i></b>&#8221;<b style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i>).&#160;</i></b>The EPS on common stock has been computed pursuant to the guidance in FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">260,</em> <i>Earnings Per Share</i>.&#160;The guidance requires the classification of the Company&#8217;s unvested restricted stock, which contains rights to receive non-forfeitable dividends, as participating securities requiring the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-class method of computing net income per share of common stock.&#160;In accordance with the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-class method, earnings per share have&#160;been computed by dividing the net income less net income attributable to unvested restricted shares by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding less unvested restricted shares. Diluted earnings per share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average shares of common stock and potentially dilutive securities outstanding in accordance with the treasury stock method.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Dilutive common stock equivalents include the dilutive effect of in-the-money stock equivalents, which are calculated based on the average share price for each period using the treasury stock method, excluding any common stock equivalents if their effect would be anti-dilutive. In periods in which a net loss has been incurred, all potentially dilutive common stock shares are considered anti-dilutive and thus are excluded from the calculation.&#160;Securities that are excluded from the calculation of weighted average dilutive common stock, because their inclusion would have been antidilutive, are:</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationVariableInterestEntityPolicy" id="c146055756" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">Variable Interest Entity.&#160;</span></i></b>We determine whether an entity is a Variable Interest Entity ("VIE") and, if so, whether it should be consolidated by utilizing judgments and estimates that are inherently subjective. Our determination of whether an entity in which we hold a direct or indirect variable interest is a VIE is based on several factors, including whether we participated in the design of the entity and whether&#160;the entity&#8217;s total equity investment at risk upon inception is sufficient to finance the entity&#8217;s activities without additional subordinated financial support. We make judgments regarding the sufficiency of the equity at risk based <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> on a qualitative analysis, and then a quantitative analysis, if necessary.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We analyze any investments in VIEs to determine if we are the primary beneficiary. In evaluating whether we are the primary beneficiary, we evaluate our direct and indirect economic interests in the entity. A reporting entity is determined to be the primary beneficiary if it holds a controlling financial interest in the VIE. Determining which reporting entity, if any, has a controlling financial interest in a VIE is primarily a qualitative approach focused on identifying which reporting entity has both: (i) the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most significantly impact such entity&#8217;s economic performance; and (ii) the obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits from such entity that could potentially be significant to such entity. Performance of that analysis requires the exercise of judgment.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We consider a variety of factors in identifying the entity that holds the power to direct matters that most significantly impact the VIE&#8217;s economic performance, including, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, the ability to direct operating decisions and activities. In addition, we consider the rights of other investors to participate in those decisions. We determine whether we are the primary beneficiary of a VIE at the time we become involved with a variable interest entity and reconsider that conclusion continually.&#160;We consolidate any VIE of which we are the primary beneficiary.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:PriorPeriodReclassificationAdjustmentDescription" id="c146055757" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b>Reclassifications</b></i>.&#160;Certain prior year balance sheet, statement of operations and statement of cash flows accounts have been reclassified to conform with the current year presentation. The reclassifications did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> affect net income in the prior year's consolidated statement of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SubsequentEventsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055758" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Subsequent Events. </span></i></b><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">We evaluate subsequen</span><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">t events up until the date the consolidated financial statements are issued.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c146055759" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Recently Issued and Adopted Accounting Pronouncements.</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2024, </em>the SEC issued final climate-disclosure rules to enhance and standardize climate&#8208;related disclosures by public companies. With regards to financial statements, the rules requires disclosure of (i)&#160;capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses incurred as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions, subject to applicable <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> percent and de minimis disclosure thresholds; (ii)&#160;capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, and losses related to carbon offsets and renewable energy credits or certificates (RECs)&#160;if used as a material component of a company's plans to achieve its disclosed climate-related targets or goals; and (iii) if the estimates and assumptions the company uses to produce the financial statements were materially impacted by risks and uncertainties associated with severe weather events and other natural conditions or any disclosed climate-related targets or transition plans, a qualitative description of how the development of such estimates and assumptions was impacted. The rules are effective for annual periods beginning <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025 </em>and are to be applied prospectively. On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 4, 2024, </em>the SEC voluntarily stayed the rules pending judicial review as a result of litigation. On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 27, 2025, </em>the SEC voted to end its defense of the rules requiring disclosure of climate-related risks and greenhouse gas emissions.&#160;However, the Eighth Circuit <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>still rule on the legal challenges to the rules, and if so could decide to uphold the rules in whole or in part or remand them to the SEC for further consideration.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> <i>Income Statement</i>&#8212;<i>Reporting Comprehensive, Income</i>&#8212;<i>Expense Disaggregation Disclosures, Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i> (&#8220;ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03&#8221;</em>).&#160;This ASU is to improve the disclosures about a public business entity&#8217;s expenses and address requests from investors for more detailed information about the types of expenses (including purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation, amortization, and depletion) in commonly presented expense captions (such as cost of sales, SG&amp;A, and research and development).&#160;The amendments in this ASU are effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption is permitted.&#160;In <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2025, </em>this was updated by ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01&#8212;Income</em> Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income&#8212;Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Clarifying the Effective Date.&#160;The amendment in this Update amends the effective date of Update <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> to clarify that all public business entities are required to adopt the guidance in annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption of Update <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> is permitted.&#160;We have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> and are currently evaluating the impact on our financial statement disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> - <i>Interim Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>),</i> which focuses on improving interim reporting guidance by clarifying requirements and enhancing navigability for entities preparing interim financial statements under GAAP.&#160;This aims to improve the guidance in Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270,</em> Interim Reporting, by enhancing the clarity and navigability of the required interim disclosures. This introduces the Disclosure Principle, requiring entities to disclose events that have a material impact on the entity since the end of the last annual reporting period. Additionally, ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> creates a comprehensive list of required interim disclosures, consolidating them into Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em> rather than having them dispersed across various Codification Topics. For public entities, the update is effective for interim reporting periods within annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>For all other entities, it is effective for interim reporting periods within annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2028. </em>Early adoption is permitted for all entities. While we are currently evaluating the impact of this pronouncement, we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect it will have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</p>

(&#8220;NRMH&#8221;) and its Lender has a covenant for a Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio&#160;(&#8220;FCCR&#8221;) as defined for NRMH as of any date that equals (a) the sum of (i) EBITDA for the period ended as of such date minus (ii) distributions for the period ended as of such date divided by (b) the sum of (i) principal payments paid for the period ended as of such date plus (ii) interest expense for period ended as of such date.&#160;The FCCR is to be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> less than <ix:nonFraction id="c146049646" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-MortgageNotesMember_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomeMember" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:DebtInstrumentCovenantMinimumFixedChargeCoverageRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.10</ix:nonFraction> to <em style="font: inherit;">1.00,</em> tested at the end of each fiscal quarter.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, NRMH was in compliance with this covenant.&#160;The Company and standalone&#160;subsidiaries have&#160;other various quarterly and annual reporting requirements&#160;to the individual property lenders and the Company is in compliance with all material conditions and covenants on those mortgage notes payable as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, with the exception for Dakota Center's loan maturity.&#160;</p>

While there can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that a material environmental liability does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exist, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently aware of any environmental liability with respect to the properties that would have a material effect on the Company's financial condition, results of operations and cash flow. Further, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> aware of any environmental liability or any unasserted claim or assessment with respect to an environmental liability that the Company believes would require additional disclosure or recording of a loss contingency.</p>

Additionally, the economic and geopolitical ramifications of the military conflicts in the&#160;Middle East&#160;and&#160;Ukraine, including sanctions, retaliatory sanctions, nationalism, supply chain disruptions and other consequences,&#160;could impact commercial real estate fundamentals and result in lower occupancy, lower rental rates, and declining values in our real estate portfolio and in the collateral securing our loan investments. We have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently experienced a direct material impact to our Company or operations; however, we will continue to monitor the financial markets for events that could impact our commercial real estate properties.</p>
