   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 20, 2024, </em>the Company&#160;entered into an underwriting agreement&#160;with The Benchmark Company, LLC&#160;pursuant to which the Company issued and sold in an underwritten public offering <ix:nonFraction id="c146049893" contextRef="d_2024-06-20_2024-06-24_CounterpartyNameAxis-TheBenchmarkCompanyLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-UnderwrittenPublicOfferingMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">109,054</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s Series D Preferred Stock.&#160;The shares of Series D Preferred Stock were sold to the public at a price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049894" contextRef="i_2024-06-24_CounterpartyNameAxis-TheBenchmarkCompanyLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-UnderwrittenPublicOfferingMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:SharesIssuedPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">16.00</ix:nonFraction> per share. The Company agreed to an underwriting discount of <ix:nonFraction id="c146049895" contextRef="i_2024-06-24_CounterpartyNameAxis-TheBenchmarkCompanyLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-UnderwrittenPublicOfferingMember" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:EquityOfferingUnderwritingDiscountPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">7</ix:nonFraction>% of the public offering price of the shares of Series D Preferred Stock sold in the offering. The offering closed on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 24, 2024, </em>generating gross proceeds of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049896" contextRef="d_2024-06-20_2024-06-24_CounterpartyNameAxis-TheBenchmarkCompanyLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-UnderwrittenPublicOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="sqft:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfPreferredStockAndPreferenceStockGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">1.74</ix:nonFraction> million, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses payable by the Company. The Company has used the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate and working capital purposes, including the acquisition of additional properties.&#160;Below are some of the key terms of the Series D Preferred Stock:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: left;"><span style="font-size:10pt"><i>Dividends:</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:10pt">Holders of shares of the Series D Preferred Stock are entitled to receive cumulative cash dividends at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c146049897" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">9.375</ix:nonFraction>% per annum of the $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049898" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockLiquidationPreference" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">25.00</ix:nonFraction> per share liquidation preference (equivalent to $<ix:nonFraction id="c146049899" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePerDollarAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.34375</ix:nonFraction> per annum per share). Dividends are payable monthly on the <em style="font: inherit;">15th</em> day of each month (each, a "Dividend Payment Date"), provided that if any Dividend Payment Date is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a business day, then the dividend that would otherwise have been payable on that Dividend Payment Date <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be paid on the next succeeding business day without adjustment in the amount of the dividend.&#160;</span>&#160;If the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> declare a dividend in a given period, an accrual is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded on the balance sheet. However, undeclared preferred stock dividends are reflected in earnings per share as discussed in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">260</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">45</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11.</em> Preferred stock dividends that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> declared accumulate and are added to the liquidation preference as of the scheduled payment date for the respective series of the preferred stock</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><i>Voting Rights:</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">Holders of shares of the Series D Preferred Stock will generally have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> voting rights. However, if the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> pay dividends on the Series D Preferred Stock for <em style="font: inherit;">eighteen</em> or more monthly dividend periods (whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consecutive), the holders of the Series D Preferred Stock (voting separately as a class with the holders of all other classes or series of the Company's preferred stock it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue upon which like voting rights have been conferred and are exercisable and which are entitled to vote as a class with the Series D Preferred Stock in the election referred to below) will be entitled to vote for the election of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049913">two</span> additional directors to serve on the Company's Board of Directors until the Company pays, or declares and sets apart funds for the payment of, all dividends that it owes on the Series D Preferred Stock, subject to certain limitations.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">In addition, the affirmative vote of the holders of at least <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146049914">two</span>-thirds of the outstanding shares of Series D Preferred Stock (voting together as a class with all other series of parity preferred stock the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue upon which like voting rights have been conferred and are exercisable) is required at any time for the Company to (i) authorize or issue any class or series of its stock ranking senior to the Series D Preferred Stock with respect to the payment of dividends or the distribution of assets on liquidation, dissolution or winding up or (ii) to amend any provision of the Company charter so as to materially and adversely affect any rights of the Series D Preferred Stock or to take certain other actions.&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><i>Liquidation Preference</i>:</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">In the event of the Company's voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up, the holders of shares of Series D Preferred Stock will be entitled to be paid out of the assets the Company has legally available for distribution to its stockholders, subject to the preferential rights of the holders of any class or series of its stock the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue ranking senior to the Series D Preferred Stock with respect to the distribution of assets upon liquidation, dissolution or winding up, a liquidation preference of <em style="font: inherit;">$25.00</em> per share, plus any accumulated and unpaid dividends to, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> including, the date of payment, before any distribution of assets is made to holders of the Company's common stock or any other class or series of the Company's stock it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue that ranks junior to the Series D Preferred Stock as to liquidation rights.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">In the event that, upon any such voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up, the Company's available assets are insufficient to pay the amount of the liquidating distributions on all outstanding shares of Series D Preferred Stock and the corresponding amounts payable on all shares of other classes or series of the Company's stock that it issues ranking on parity with the Series D Preferred Stock in the distribution of assets, then the holders of the Series D Preferred Stock and all other such classes or series of stock shall share ratably in any such distribution of assets in proportion to the full liquidating distributions to which they would otherwise be respectively entitled.</span></p>

   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Cash Dividends on Common Stock and Preferred Stock.&#160;</i></b></span>For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>,&#160;the&#160;Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050001">not</span> declare&#160;a cash dividend on shares of Series A Common Stock.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 28, 2026, </em>the&#160;Board of Directors has suspended the Company&#8217;s monthly dividend on its Series D Preferred Stock commencing with the <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026 </em>monthly dividend that would have been paid on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 15, 2026. </em>In accordance with the terms of the Series D Preferred Stock, the unpaid monthly dividends will continue to accrue at $<ix:nonFraction id="c146050002" contextRef="d_2026-01-28_2026-01-28_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePerDollarAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.19531</ix:nonFraction> per share each month. Under the guidance of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">260</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">45</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11,</em> if the Company's Board of Directors do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> declare a dividend in a given period, an accrual is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded on the balance sheet, however; undeclared preferred stock dividends are reflected in earnings per share. Preferred stock dividends that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> declared accumulate and are added to the liquidation preference as of the scheduled payment date for the respective series of the preferred stock.&#160;The Board and the Company intend to reassess, on a quarterly basis, when accrued dividends on the Series D Preferred Stock <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be paid and when the monthly dividend payments can be reinstated.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Partnership Interests. </i></b>Through the Company, its subsidiaries, and its partnerships, we own <ix:nonFraction id="c146050014" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-CommercialPropertyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">8</ix:nonFraction> commercial properties in fee interest, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050015">two</span> of which we own partial interests in through our holdings in various affiliates in which we serve as general partner, member and/or manager. Each of the limited partnerships is referred to as a "DownREIT." In each DownREIT, we have the right, through put and call options, to require our co-investors to exchange their interests for shares of our Common Stock at a stated price after a defined period (generally <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> years from the date they <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> invested in the entity's real property), the occurrence of a specified event or a combination thereof. The Company is a limited partner in <ix:nonFraction id="c146050018" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:NumberOfLimitedPartnershipsInWhichCompanyIsSoleGeneralPartner" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">five</ix:nonFraction> partnerships and sole stockholder in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> corporation, which entities purchase and leaseback model homes from homebuilders.</span></p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">12.</em> SHARE-BASED INCENTIVE PLAN</b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">The Company maintains a restricted stock incentive plan for the purpose of attracting and retaining officers, employees, and non-employee Board members. Share awards generally vest in equal annual installments over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050057">three</span>-to-<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050058">ten</span>-year period from date of issuance. Non-vested shares have voting rights and are eligible for any dividends paid on shares of common stock. The Company recognized compensation cost for these fixed awards over the service vesting period, which represents the requisite service period, using the straight-line method. Prior to our IPO, the value of non-vested shares was calculated based on the offering price of the shares in the most recent private placement offering of $<ix:nonFraction id="c146050059" contextRef="i_2006-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:SharesIssuedPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">20.00</ix:nonFraction>, adjusted for stock dividends since granted and assumed selling costs, which management believed approximated fair market value as of the date of grant. Upon our IPO, the value of non-vested shares granted is generally calculated based on the closing price of our common stock on the date of the grant.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><b><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"><em style="font: inherit;">13.</em> SEGMENTS</span></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s reportable segments consist of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050099">three</span> types of real estate properties for which the Company&#8217;s chief operating decision maker (CODM), which is our Chief Executive Officer,&#160;has the final decision when allocating capital and personnel to the various segments,&#160;internally&#160;evaluate operating performance and financial results: Office/Industrial Properties, Model Home Properties and Retail Properties. The Company also has certain corporate-level activities including accounting, finance, legal administration, and management information systems which are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered separate operating segments.&#160;There is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material inter-segment activity.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The CODM evaluates the performance of our&#160;segments based upon an internal net operating income (&#8220;NOI&#8221;), which is a non-GAAP supplemental financial measure on a quarterly basis as disclosed in the <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Qs and <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Ks. We believe that NOI is a widely accepted measure of comparative operating performance in the real estate community. However, our use of the term NOI <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be comparable to that of other real estate companies as they <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have different methodologies for computing this amount.&#160;The Company defines NOI for its segments as operating revenues (rental income, tenant reimbursements, parking income, and other operating income, net of provision for bad debt) less rental operating costs (property operating expenses, real estate taxes, insurance, utilities, repairs and maintenance, and asset management fees) excluding interest expense. NOI excludes certain items that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered to be controllable in connection with the management of an asset such as non-property income &amp; expenses, depreciation &amp; amortization, real estate acquisition fees &amp; expenses, non-cash impairments and corporate general &amp; administrative expenses. Quarterly, the Company reviews and tests for non-cash impairments, as required by GAAP, on all our properties (i.e., Office/Industrial Properties,&#160;Retail Properties, and Model Home Properties); however, the CODM does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consider those non-cash impairments with evaluating the segment&#8217;s cash operations and NOI.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The CODM uses NOI to evaluate and assess each segments' performance and in deciding how to allocate resources.&#160;For Model Home performance, the CODM also includes the gain or loss on sale of real estate assets net of any impairments, because we believe that is a major component in the operating success of the segment and part of the business model for Model Homes.&#160;The gain on sale of model homes resulted in cash flows to the Company that the CODM can decide on how to allocate to future operations.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The following tables compare the Company&#8217;s segment activity and NOI and adjusted NOI for Model Home income&#160;to its results of operations and financial position as of and for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively.&#160;The line items listed in the below NOI tables include the significant expense considered by the CODM for cash allocations on future investments.&#160;The Other Non-Segment &amp; Consolidating Items represent corporate activity, the investment in Conduit, and other eliminating items for consolidation.&#160;The information for Corporate and Other are presented to reconcile back to the consolidated statement of operations, but is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered a reportable segment.&#160;This includes the loss on Conduit marketable securities.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Since a significant portion of the total operating expense for Retail and Office/Industrial are recouped as part of recovery revenue, the CODM looks at NOI as a whole when reviewing the segments.&#160;For the Model Home segment, the properties are leased on a triple net basis and the tenants are responsible for a significant portion of the operating expenses.&#160;Therefore, the CODM focuses on Model Home revenue, any impairments and the gain on sale of model homes.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The CODM reviews on a regular basis the GAAP performance of each segment, including the significant segment expenses reported for GAAP shown in the table below. Our significant segment expenses include consolidated expense categories presented in our consolidated statements of operations, as well as rental operating costs.&#160;This information is provided to the CODM and factors into the CODM&#8217;s decision making for company-wide strategy. The following tables compare the Company&#8217;s segment activity and&#160;to its results of GAAP operations and financial position&#160;for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively.&#160;The information for Corporate and Other are presented to reconcile back to the consolidated statement of operations, but is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered a reportable segment as noted above.</p>

   <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;"><span style="font-size:10pt"><b><a id="Note_14" title="Note 14" href="#"></a><em style="font: inherit;">14.</em> INCOME TAX PROVISION</b></span></p>
   <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have elected to be taxed as a REIT under the Internal Revenue Code of <em style="font: inherit;">1986,</em> as amended, commencing with the taxable year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2000. </em>As a REIT, U.S. federal income tax law generally requires us to distribute annually at least <em style="font: inherit;">90%</em> of our REIT taxable income, without regard to the deduction for dividends paid and excluding net capital gains, and that we pay tax at regular corporate rates to the extent that we annually distribute less than <em style="font: inherit;">100%</em> of our net taxable income. We are also subject to U.S. federal, state and local income taxes on our domestic taxable REIT subsidiaries ("TRS") based on the tax jurisdictions in which they operate.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we recorded a current income tax provision(benefit) of $<ix:nonFraction id="c146050485" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">18,057</ix:nonFraction> and $(<ix:nonFraction id="c146050486" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF" sign="-">25,409</ix:nonFraction>) related to activities of our taxable REIT subsidiaries. There was a $<ix:nonFraction id="c146050487" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsNet" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">223,388</ix:nonFraction> income tax asset related to the operating activities of our TRS entities as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have calculated the provision for income taxes during interim reporting periods by applying an estimate of the annual effective tax rate for the projected full fiscal year to the TRS pretax income or loss excluding unusual or infrequently occurring discrete items for the reporting period, and have accounted for the REIT's minimum state income taxes as a discrete item&#160;in the reporting period.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> "Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures" ("ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09"</em>). ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> intends to improve the transparency of income tax disclosures. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2024 </em>and is to be adopted on a prospective basis with the option to apply retrospectively. The Company adopted the disclosures on a prospective basis which did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> create a material impact to our consolidated financial statements.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">We own three commercial properties located in Colorado, three in North Dakota, one in Southern California, one in Texas and one in Maryland. Our model home properties are located in four&#160;states. While geographical clustering of real estate enables us to reduce our operating costs through economies of scale by servicing several&#160;properties with less staff, it makes us susceptible to changing market conditions in&#160;these discrete geographic areas.&#160;We do not develop properties but acquire properties that are stabilized or that we anticipate will be stabilized within two or three years of acquisition. We consider a property to be stabilized once it has achieved an 80% occupancy rate for a full year&#160;as of January 1 of such year or has been operating for three years.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">Most of our office and retail properties are leased to a variety of tenants ranging from small businesses to large public companies, many of which are not investment grade. We have, in the past, entered into, and intend in the future to enter into, purchase agreements for real estate having net leases that require the tenant to pay all of the operating expenses or pay increases in operating expenses over specific base years. Most of our office leases are for terms of three to five years with annual rental increases. Our model homes are typically leased back for two to three years to the home builder on a triple-net lease.&#160;Under a triple-net lease, the tenant is required to pay all operating, maintenance and insurance costs and real estate taxes with respect to the leased property.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">We seek to diversify our portfolio by commercial real estate segments, including office, industrial, retail and model home properties&#160;to reduce the adverse effect of a single under-performing segment&#160;and/or tenant. We further mitigate risk&#160;at the tenant level through our credit review process, which varies by tenant class.&#160;For example, our commercial and industrial tenants tend to be corporations or individually owned businesses.&#160;In these cases, we typically obtain financial records, including financial statements and tax returns (depending on the circumstance), and run credit reports for any prospective tenant to support our decision to enter into a rental arrangement. We also typically obtain security deposits from these commercial tenants. Our Model Home commercial tenants are well-known homebuilders with established credit histories. These tenants are subjected to financial review and analysis prior to us entering into a sales-leaseback transaction.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In June 2024, the Board of Directors established the Strategic Planning and Cyber Committee (the "Strategic Committee"). The purpose of the Strategic Committee is to: assist the Board in carrying out its responsibilities of oversight over the Company's business strategy, make recommendations to the Board on the Company's strategic direction and objectives and serve as a liaison between the Board and management, and assist the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities of oversight with regard to the Company's identification, assessment, and management of the Company's cybersecurity risks. There can be no assurance that the work of the Strategic Committee will result in any transaction being pursued or consummated. In addition, there is no formal timetable for the Strategic Committee's exploration of potential strategic alternatives, and the Company does not intend to disclose any developments with respect to the Strategic Committee's activities unless and until the Company determines that further disclosure is appropriate or required by law or regulation.</p>

Stockholders' Equity in&#160;the Notes to the&#160;Consolidated Financial Statements in "Part I, Item 1. Financial Statements" of this Quarterly Report.</p>

  <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><b>CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES</b></span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">There have been no material changes to our critical accounting policies as previously disclosed in our 2025</span>&#160;year-end&#160;Annual Report<span style="font-size: 10pt;">.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><b>MANAGEMENT EVALUATION OF RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</b></span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">Management&#8217;s evaluation of operating results includes an assessment of our ability to generate the cash flow necessary to pay operating expenses, general and administrative expenses, debt service and to fund distributions to our stockholders. As a result, management&#8217;s assessment of operating results gives less emphasis to the effects of unrealized gains and losses and other non-cash charges, such as depreciation and amortization and impairment charges, which may cause fluctuations in net income for comparable periods but have no impact on cash flows. Management&#8217;s evaluation of our potential for generating cash flow includes assessments of our recently acquired properties, our non-stabilized properties, long-term sustainability of our real estate portfolio, our future operating cash flow from anticipated acquisitions, and the proceeds from the sales of our real estate assets.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">In addition, management evaluates the results of the operations of our portfolio and individual properties with a primary focus on increasing and enhancing the value, quality and quantity of properties in our real estate holdings. Management focuses its efforts on improving underperforming assets through re-leasing efforts, including negotiation of lease renewals and rental rates. Properties are regularly evaluated for potential added value appreciation and cashflow and, if lacking such potential, are sold with the equity reinvested in new acquisitions or otherwise allocated in a manner we believe is accretive to our stockholders.&#160;Our ability to increase assets under management is affected by our ability to raise borrowings and/or capital, coupled with our ability to identify appropriate investments.</span></p>
  <div>
    &#160;

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="text-transform:uppercase; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt"><b>RESULTS OF OPERATIONS FOR THE THREE MONTHS ENDED March 31, 2026 and 2025</b></span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Revenues.</i></b>&#160;Total revenues were approximately&#160;$3.8 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to approximately&#160;$4.1 million&#160;for the same period in 2025.&#160;As of March 31, 2026, we had approximately&#160;$100.5 million&#160;in net real estate assets including&#160;75&#160;model homes, compared to approximately $117.4 million&#160;in net real estate assets, including&#160;84 model homes at&#160;March 31, 2025.&#160;The average number of model homes held during the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025 was approximately 78&#160;and 81, respectively.&#160;The change in revenue is directly related to the decrease&#160;in commercial real estate&#160;rental income during the current period from the sale of Dakota Center.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Rental Operating Costs.</i></b>&#160;Rental operating costs totaled approximately&#160;$1.5 million&#160;for the<b><i>&#160;</i></b>three months ended<b><i> </i></b>March 31, 2026,<b><i> </i></b>compared to&#160;approximately&#160;$1.6 million&#160;for the same period in 2025.&#160;Rental operating costs as a percentage of total revenue was approximately 35% and 39% for the&#160;three<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt"> months ended </span>March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>General and Administrative Expenses.</i></b>&#160;G&amp;A&#160;expenses for the<b><i>&#160;</i></b>three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025&#160;totaled approximately&#160;$1.7 million&#160;and&#160;$1.7 million,&#160;respectively.&#160;G&amp;A expenses as a percentage of total revenue was&#160;44.4% <span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">and&#160;40.3%&#160;</span>for the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. G&amp;A expenses for the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;remained constant compared to the same period ending in 2025; however, the Company is actively looking to reduce G&amp;A expenses during the year. There has been a reduction of employee headcount during the first quarter of 2026 with more expected this year. Starting in April 2026, the Chief Executive Officer has agreed to a voluntary 5% reduction in his annual salary. Additionally, the Board of Directors have approved the reduction by one Director starting in June 2026, which will provide additional G&amp;A savings.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">Depreciation and Amortization.</span></i></b><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;Depreciation and amortization expense was&#160;</span>approximately&#160;$1.0 million&#160;and&#160;$1.2 million <span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">for the&#160;</span>three<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt"> months ended </span>March 31, 2026 and 2025<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">, respectively. The decrease in depreciation and amortization expense is&#160;</span>directly related to the decrease&#160;in commercial real estate&#160;rental income during the current period, from the sale of Dakota Center and the placement of Shea Center into receivership and listed as held for sale.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Asset Impairments</i></b>.&#160;We review the carrying value of each of our real estate properties regularly&#160;to determine if circumstances indicate an impairment in the carrying value of these investments exists. During the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, we recognized&#160;non-cash impairment charges of approximately&#160;$524,373&#160;and&#160;$26,943, respectively.&#160; Approximately $0.4 million of the impairment charge for the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, was related to the Shea Center II.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">Interest Expense - mortgage notes.</span></i></b><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;Interest expense, including amortization of deferred finance charges was&#160;</span>approximately&#160;$2.1 million <span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">for the&#160;</span>three months ended March 31, 2026<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">,&#160;compared to&#160;</span>approximately&#160;$1.5 million <span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">for the same period in </span>2025<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">.</span><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;T</span><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">he weighted average interest rate on our outstanding debt was&#160;</span>6.29%<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;and 5.83%</span><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;as of </span>March 31, 2026 and 2025<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">, respectively.&#160;Mortgage notes payable totaled approximately&#160;$82.4 million&#160;and $94.4&#160;million as of </span>March 31, 2026 and 2025<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">, respectively. While mortgage interest expenses increased over the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025</span>, approximately $0.7 million of the interest expense attributed to <span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">the&#160;</span>three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;was related to one-time charge for the default interest on the loan for Dakota Center. Management expects future interest expenses to continue to decrease going forward for the year ended 2026.&#160; Additionally, during the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026, we recorded defaulted interest expense of approximately $0.1 million related to the Shea Center II loan.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">Gain (Loss)&#160;on Sale of Real Estate Assets, net.</span></i></b><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;The change in gain or loss on the sale of real estate assets is dependent on the mix of properties sold</span><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt"> and the market conditions at the time of the sale. S</span><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">ee "Significant Transactions in </span>2026<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt"> and </span>2025<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">" above for further detail.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">Income allocated to non-controlling interests.</span></i></b><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;Income allocated to non-controlling interests for the&#160;</span>three<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt"> months ended </span>March 31, 2026<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;and&#160;</span>2025<span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">&#160;totaled approximately $0.1 million&#160;</span><span style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size:10pt">and&#160;$0.1 million, respectively.&#160;This was directly related to&#160;the gain on sales of model homes held by&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">our&#160;affiliated limited partnerships.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Loss&#160;on Conduit remeasurement</b></i>.&#160;As of March 31, 2026, we&#160;held&#160;709,000 public common stock warrants of CDTTW, and 540,000 private common stock warrants, with a combined value of approximately&#160;$5,885.&#160;Conduit's&#160;public common stock warrants (CDTTW)&#160;and Private CDT Warrants presented on the&#160;consolidated balance sheets were measured at fair value using Level 1 and Level 3 market prices, taking into account the adoption of ASU 2022-03 <i>Fair Value Measurement of Equity Securities Subject to Contractual Sale Restrictions.</i></p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL RESOURCES</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Overview</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our anticipated future sources of liquidity may include existing cash and cash equivalents, cash flows from operations, refinancing of existing mortgages, future real estate sales, new borrowings from our model home lines of credit,&#160;and the sale of our equity or issuance of debt securities or bonds. Our cash and restricted cash at March 31, 2026 was approximately&#160;$5.2 million.&#160;Our future capital needs include paying down existing borrowings, maintaining our existing properties, funding tenant improvements, paying lease commissions (to the extent they are not covered by lender-held reserve deposits), and the payment of dividends to our stockholders. We also are actively seeking model home investments that are likely to produce income and achieve long-term gains in order to pay dividends to our stockholders. To ensure that we can effectively execute these objectives, we routinely review our liquidity requirements and continually evaluate all potential sources of liquidity.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our short-term liquidity needs include paying our current operating costs, satisfying the debt service requirements of our existing mortgages, completing tenant improvements, paying leasing commissions, and funding dividends to stockholders.&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt;">Future principal payments due on mortgage notes payable, during the last three months of&#160;2026&#160;and in the year ending&#160;December 31, 2026 total approximately </span>$20.4 million<span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;and&#160;$2.4 million, respectively, of which&#160;</span>$3.8 million<span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;in 2025&#160;and $2.0 million&#160;in 2026&#160;are&#160;related to model home properties.&#160;</span>The&#160;non-recourse&#160;loan for Shea Center matured on January 5, 2026.&#160;On January 14, 2026 the Dakota Center property sold to an unrelated third-party for approximately $4.7 million, net of selling costs. The lender received approximately $4.3 million from the sale of the property, which was applied to settle the net loan balance of approximately $8.9 million.&#160;The Company was not responsible for the remaining balance on this non-recourse loan, and the transaction resulted in a net gain of approximately $3.4 million.&#160;No other commercial property loans mature during 2026.&#160;</p>
  <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
   <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: justify;">
     &#160;
   </div>
   <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: justify;">
     On January 21, 2026,&#160;the Company and NetREIT SC II, LLC, a subsidiary of the Company (the &#8220;Borrower&#8221; or "Shea Center"), received a notice (the &#8220;Default Notice&#8221;) from Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (the &#8220;Lender&#8221;) alleging that the Borrower&#8217;s failure to repay in full by January 5, 2026 the indebtedness owed under that certain promissory note dated as of December 24, 2015 issued to The Bancorp Bank (the &#8220;Original Lender&#8221;) in the original principal amount of $17,727,500&#160;(the &#8220;Note&#8221;), the related loan agreement, dated as of December 24, 2015 by and between Borrower and the Original Lender (the &#8220;Loan Agreement&#8221;) and other related agreements (together with the Note and the Loan Agreement, the &#8220;Loan Documents&#8221;), constituted an event of default under the Loan Documents.&#160;
    <div style="font-size: 10pt;">
      As a result of the alleged event of default, the entire unpaid amounts shall bear interest at the default interest rate equal to the lesser&#160;of (i) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, or (ii) 5% above the original interest rate of 4.92% per annum.
    </div>
    <div style="font-size: 10pt;">
      &#160;
    </div>
    <div style="font-size: 10pt;">
      In addition, the Lender has the right to foreclose or partially foreclose certain real and personal property that the Borrower had pledged as security for the Note located in Douglas County, Colorado, known as the &#8220;Shea Center II&#8221; (the &#8220;Property&#8221;).&#160;The Default Notice further states that the Lender revoked the Borrower&#8217;s license under the Loan Documents to receive, collect and make use of rents, profits and income from the Property.
    </div>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">While we will continue to pursue value creating investments, the Board of Directors believes there is significant embedded value in our assets that is yet to be realized by the market. In December 2024, the Board of Directors authorized a stock repurchase program of up to $6.0 million of outstanding shares of our Series A Common Stock and up to $4.0 million of our Series D Preferred Stock, which the Board of Directors&#160;did not renew&#160;in December 2025.&#160;During the&#160;year ended December 31, 2025, we&#160;repurchased 16,080 shares of our Series A Common Stock, with an average price of $4.79 per share, including a commission of $0.025 per share, for a total cost of $77,092 for the Series A Common Stock.&#160;This does not include the shares repurchased in the fixed price self-tender offer (the "Tender Offer") during April-May 2025.&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2025,&#160;the Company repurchased 23,346&#160;shares of our Series D Preferred Stock at an average price of approximately $14.76&#160;per share, including a commission of $0.035 per share, for a total cost of $344,503 for the&#160;Series D Preferred Stock. Any repurchased shares are treated as authorized and unissued in accordance with Maryland law and shown as a reduction of stockholders&#8217; equity at cost.&#160;There were no repurchases&#160;of&#160;Series A Common Stock or&#160;Series D Preferred Stock during&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;as there were no repurchase plans in place.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">There can be no assurance that the Company will refinance loans,&#160;take out&#160;additional&#160;financing or that capital will be available to the Company on acceptable terms, if at all. If events or circumstances occur such that the Company does not obtain additional funding, it will most likely be required to reduce its plans, reduce certain discretionary spending or even sell properties, which could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s ability to achieve its intended business objectives. We believe that cash on hand, cash flow from our existing portfolio, distributions from joint ventures in Model Home Partnerships and property sales during&#160;2025&#160;and 2026&#160;will be sufficient to fund our operating costs, planned capital expenditures and required dividends for at least the next twelve months. If our cash flow from operating activities is not sufficient to fund our short-term liquidity needs, we plan to fund a portion of these needs from additional borrowings of secured or unsecured indebtedness, from real estate sales, issuance of debt instruments, additional investors, or we may reduce or suspend the rate of dividends to our stockholders.</p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our long-term liquidity needs include the capital&#160;necessary to grow and maintain our portfolio of investments. We believe that the potential financing capital available to us in the future is sufficient to fund our long-term liquidity needs.&#160;We are continually reviewing our existing portfolio to determine which properties have met our short- and long-term goals and while seeking to&#160;reinvest&#160;the proceeds in properties with better potential to increase performance.&#160;We expect to obtain additional cash in connection with refinancing of maturing mortgages and assumption of existing debt collateralized by some or all of our real property in the future to meet our long-term liquidity needs.&#160;If we are unable to arrange a line of credit, borrow on properties, privately place securities or sell securities to the public, we may not be able to acquire additional properties to meet our long-term objectives.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026,&#160;the&#160;Company did not declare&#160;a cash dividend on shares of Series A Common Stock. For the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026, the Company did not declare and did not pay dividends on shares of Series D Preferred Stock. As of January 28, 2026, the&#160;Board of Directors has suspended the Company&#8217;s monthly dividend on its Series D Preferred Stock commencing with the January 2026 monthly dividend that would have been paid on February 15, 2026. Since&#160;the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors did&#160;not declare a dividend during the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026, an accrual was&#160;not recorded on the balance sheet. However, undeclared preferred stock dividends are reflected in earnings per share as discussed in ASC 260-10-45-11. In accordance with the terms of the Series D Preferred Stock,&#160;Preferred stock dividends that are not declared accumulate and are added to the liquidation preference as of the scheduled payment date for the respective series of the preferred stock.&#160;No interest, or sum of money in lieu of interest, is payable in respect of any dividend payments on the Series D Preferred Stock that are in arrears.&#160;As of March 31, 2026&#160;and December 31, 2025, the cumulative preferred dividends in arrears on the Series D preferred stock was $0.6 million and $0, respectively.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Board and the Company intend to reassess, on a quarterly basis, when accrued dividends on the Series D Preferred Stock may be paid and when the monthly dividend payments can be reinstated. Under the guidance of ASC 260-10-45-11, if the Company's Board of Directors do not declare a dividend in a given period, an accrual is not recorded on the balance sheet, however; undeclared preferred stock dividends are reflected in earnings per share. Preferred stock dividends that are not declared accumulate and are added to the liquidation preference as of the scheduled payment date for the respective series of the preferred stock.&#160;Cash permitting, the Company intends&#160;to continue to pay dividends on a monthly basis to holders of our&#160;Series D Preferred Stock&#160;going forward, but there can be no guarantee the Board of Directors will approve any future dividends.&#160;The Company has not decided when it will resume&#160;dividends to our common stockholders on a quarterly basis.&#160;As of March 31, 2026&#160;and December 31, 2025, the cumulative preferred dividends in arrears on the Series D preferred stock was $0.6 million and $0, respectively.&#160;</p>

Pursuant to the terms of the Purchase Agreement, the Company agreed to sell in a registered direct offering (the &#8220;Offering&#8221;), (i) 140,000 shares (the &#8220;Public Shares&#8221;) of its Series A Common Stock and (ii) pre-funded warrants to purchase up to 30,830 shares (the &#8220;Pre-Funded Warrant Shares&#8221;) of Series A Common Stock (the &#8220;Pre-Funded Warrants&#8221;). Each Public Share and accompanying Pre-Funded Warrant were sold together at a combined offering price of $12.00. The Pre-Funded Warrants were immediately exercisable at a nominal exercise price of $0.0001 and were exercised on July 14, 2025 in full.</p>

The Company has used and intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for working capital and for other general corporate purposes including to potentially acquire additional properties.</p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Cash Flow&#160;for the </span>three months ended March 31, 2026<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">, and </span>March 31, 2025</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Operating Activities: </span></i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Net cash used in&#160;operating activities for the </span>three months ended March 31, 2026<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">, totaled approximately </span>$1.0 million<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">, as compared to cash used in operating activities of&#160;</span>$0.1 million<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"> for the </span>three months ended March 31, 2025<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">. </span>The change in net cash used in operating activities is primarily due to the sale of Dakota Center, combined with other changes&#160;in net income, which fluctuates due&#160;to new leases, leasing renewals, tenant move outs and model home sales and acquisitions, as well as changes&#160;in non-cash addbacks or subtractions such as straight-line rent, are the primary drivers of the increase in cash used in operating activities.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Investing Activities: </span></i><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Net cash provided by&#160;investing activities for the </span>three months ended March 31, 2026<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">, was approximately </span>$6.9 million<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;compared to approximately&#160;</span>$13.6 million<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;used in investing activities during the same period in </span>2025<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">. The change&#160;from each period&#160;was primarily related to the sale of our commercial properties in February 2025 for approximately </span>$4.7 million, net of selling costs,&#160;<span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">and the sale of model home properties for approximately $7.4 million during the </span>three months ended March 31, 2026.&#160;There were no similar commercial property sales during the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2025, however, model home sales during the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2025&#160;totaled approximately $22.3 million. Cash used in&#160;real estate acquisition and capital improvement totaled approximately $0.2 million, for the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;compared to&#160;$4.8 million&#160;for the same period in 2025.</p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</i></b></p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On July 12, 2021, the Company&#160;entered into a securities purchase agreement with a single U.S. institutional investor for the purchase and sale of 100,000 shares of its Series A Common Stock, Common Stock Warrants&#160;to purchase up to 200,000 shares of Series A Common Stock and Pre-Funded Warrants&#160;to purchase up to 200,000 shares of Series A Common Stock. The Pre-Funded Warrants were exercised in full during August 2021 at a nominal exercise price of $0.10&#160;per share. The Common Stock Warrants had&#160;an exercise price of $55.00 per share,&#160;exercisable upon issuance and will expire five years from the date of&#160;issuance.&#160;In July 2025 the exercise price was adjusted to $12.00 per share and the term of the warrants extended to July 16, 2030.</p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">If all the potential Common Stock Warrants outstanding at March 31, 2026, were exercised at the price of $12 per share, gross proceeds to us would be approximately $2.4&#160;million and we would as a result issue an additional 200,000 shares of common stock.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b>Inflation</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Leases generally provide for limited increases in rent as a result of fixed increases, increases in the consumer price index (typically subject to ceilings), or increases in the clients&#8217; sales volumes. We expect that inflation will cause these lease provisions to result in rent increases over time. During times when inflation is greater than increases in rent, as provided for in the leases, rent increases may not keep up with the rate of inflation.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">However, our use of net lease agreements tends to reduce our exposure to rising property expenses due to inflation because the client is responsible for property expenses. Inflation and increased costs may have an adverse impact on our clients if increases in their operating expenses exceed increases in revenue.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><a id="quanqual" title="quanqual" href="#"></a>ITEM 3. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As a smaller reporting company, we are not required to provide disclosure pursuant to this item.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><a id="conpro" title="conpro" href="#"></a>ITEM 4. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company maintains disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in the Company's Exchange Act reports is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC's rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to the Company's management, including its Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Accounting Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure based closely on the definition of &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures&#8221; in Rule 13a-14(c). In designing and evaluating the disclosure controls and procedures, management recognized that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving the desired control objectives, and management necessarily was required to apply its judgment in evaluating the cost-benefit relationship of possible controls and procedures.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of the end of the period covered by this report, we carried out an evaluation, under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and&#160;Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures. Based upon that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and&#160;Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of the end of the period covered by this report.</p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Stock Repurchase Program</i></b>.&#160;While we will continue to pursue value creating investments, the Board of Directors believes there is significant embedded value in our assets that is yet to be realized by the market. Therefore, returning capital to stockholders through a repurchase program is an attractive use of capital currently.&#160;In December 2024, the Board of Directors authorized a stock repurchase program of up to $6.0 million of outstanding shares of our Series A Common Stock and up to $4.0 million of our Series D Preferred Stock, which the Board of Directors&#160;did not renew&#160;in December 2025.&#160;During the&#160;year ended December 31, 2025, we&#160;repurchased 16,080 shares of our Series A Common Stock, with an average price of $4.79 per share, including a commission of $0.025 per share, for a total cost of $77,092 for the Series A Common Stock.&#160;This does not include the shares repurchased in the fixed price self-tender offer (the "Tender Offer") during April-May 2025.&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2025,&#160;the Company repurchased 23,346&#160;shares of our Series D Preferred Stock at an average price of approximately $14.76&#160;per share, including a commission of $0.035 per share, for a total cost of $344,503 for the&#160;Series D Preferred Stock. Any repurchased shares are treated as authorized and unissued in accordance with Maryland law and shown as a reduction of stockholders&#8217; equity at cost.&#160;There were no repurchases&#160;of&#160;Series A Common Stock or&#160;Series D Preferred Stock during&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;as there were no repurchase plans in place.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><b><a id="defaults" title="defaults" href="#"></a>Item 3. Defaults Upon Senior Securities.</b></span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">During January 2026, the Company received notice that the Company's failure to repay in full by January 5, 2026 the indebtedness related to the loan agreement governing Shea Center II had triggered a default event. On February 13, 2026, the Company received notification that the Shea Center II property governed by the non-recourse loan agreement was moved into receivership and the lender has started the foreclosure process. The foreclosure sale and public auction is scheduled for June 17, 2026. The lender holds approximately $2.4 million in restricted cash, some of which is being utilized by the receiver to operate the property.&#160; Additionally, during the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, Shea Center II was listed as held for sale, related to the foreclosure sale and&#160;impaired approximately $0.4 million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As of January 28, 2026, the&#160;Board of Directors has suspended the Company&#8217;s monthly dividend on its Series D Preferred Stock commencing with the January 2026 monthly dividend that would have been paid on February 15, 2026. Since&#160;the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors did&#160;not declare a dividend during the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026, an accrual was&#160;not recorded on the balance sheet. However, undeclared preferred stock dividends are reflected in earnings per share as discussed in ASC 260-10-45-11. In accordance with the terms of the Series D Preferred Stock,&#160;Preferred stock dividends that are not declared accumulate and are added to the liquidation preference as of the scheduled payment date for the respective series of the preferred stock.&#160;No interest, or sum of money in lieu of interest, is payable in respect of any dividend payments on the Series D Preferred Stock that are in arrears.&#160;As of March 31, 2026&#160;and December 31, 2025, the cumulative preferred dividends in arrears on the Series D preferred stock was $0.6 million and $0, respectively.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Board and the Company intend to reassess, on a quarterly basis, when accrued dividends on the Series D Preferred Stock may be paid and when the monthly dividend payments can be reinstated. The Company has not decided when it will resume&#160;dividends to our common stockholders on a quarterly basis. As of the date of filing this quarterly report, $0.8 million in dividends are in arrears.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><b><a id="minesafe" title="minesafe" href="#"></a>Item 4. Mine Safety Disclosures</b></span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">None.&#160;</span></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>,&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050563"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050569"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050570"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c146050571">no</span></span></span></span>&#160;director or officer of the Company adopted or terminated a &#8220;Rule&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10b5</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>&#160;trading arrangement&#8221; or &#8220;non-Rule&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10b5</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>&#160;trading arrangement,&#8221; as each term is defined in Item&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">408</em>(a) of Regulation S-K.</p>
